opening_message:
Ticket 1: Richard Davis (employee ID E011) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, write is within policy (role owns the system, so admin would be permitted, but write is the requested level). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E011 as contractor with basic training (conflicts with prior note listing full_time). Contractors with basic training max at read; requested write exceeds policy, so recommend granting read.
reason: There is conflicting information about E011's employment type: HR's note says full-time Payroll Specialist (which would permit write), but Security's note says their database shows contractor with basic training, for which the maximum allowed is read. Requested write exceeds the contractor maximum, and given the unresolved conflict, the safe, policy-compliant grant is read (the most restrictive applicable maximum). Never grant more than requested is satisfied.
